Updated assessment incorporating SLOOS: The November 3, 2021 FOMC statement remains broadly constructive—ongoing recovery in activity and employment, tapering that aligns with progress toward goals, and continued policy accommodation. The Financial Stability Report tempers this with concerns about elevated valuations and vulnerability to rate repricing. However, the SLOOS points to a supportive credit backdrop: banks broadly eased lending standards across residential real estate, consumer (credit cards and autos), and CRE; increased credit limits and reduced auto loan rates; and reported stronger demand in consumer credit and parts of CRE. Foreign banks also eased CRE standards, citing improved economic outlook, competition, liquidity, and capital positions. While some pockets showed weaker demand (notably in C&I and auto at certain institutions), expectations for stronger demand in credit cards and C&I suggest improving forward credit appetite. Netting these, SLOOS corroborates “accommodative financial conditions” and offsets some FSR caution, though vulnerabilities and the risk that inflation proves persistent still warrant a guarded tone.

Bottom line: supportive with cautious undertones, nudged more positive by easier bank credit supply and firmer demand signals.
